headline: Funding flows. Risks rise. Satellites launch.
deck: This week saw a mix of funding successes and cautionary tales in satellite operations.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amidst defense push
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C funding round, emphasizing its role in co-orbital security and space domain awareness. The company’s valuation now stands at $1.6 billion, signaling strong investor confidence in defense applications. This funding is particularly timely, as the DoD increasingly prioritizes advanced space capabilities.
stories.soWhat: Investors are clearly betting that space security is the next frontier, but let's see if True Anomaly can deliver on its promises without getting lost in the bureaucracy.

stories.head: GAO flags satellite costs for Space Force
stories.body: The Government Accountability Office (GAO) has raised concerns about the escalating costs and launch risks within the Space Force's satellite portfolio. This scrutiny comes as the FY27 budget markup adds $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, indicating that lawmakers are finally waking up to the complexities of space operations.
stories.soWhat: If the GAO is worried, contractors should be too; it’s hard to justify spending when costs are ballooning and timelines are slipping.

stories.head: Pegasus rocket’s retirement party launches Swift mission
stories.body: The Pegasus rocket successfully launched the Swift reboost mission, potentially marking the end of its operational life. This mission is crucial for maintaining the Swift spacecraft's position, but it also underscores the aging fleet of air-launched rockets. The Pegasus program has faced numerous challenges, and this launch might just be the final bow.
stories.soWhat: The end of Pegasus could signal a shift in how we think about air-launched rockets; sometimes, it's just time to let go.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on True Anomaly's next moves
watchlist.body: With $190 million in new funding, True Anomaly's next steps could redefine co-orbital security strategies.

watchlist.title: Space Force budget discussions heat up

watchlist.title: Sierra Space prepares for Dream Chaser launch
watchlist.body: With the Dream Chaser DoD variant clearing its design review, a launch could be imminent, assuming they can avoid further delays.

watchlist.title: Watch for Isar Aerospace's upcoming launch
watchlist.body: Isar Aerospace is set to launch a German-built Planet imaging satellite, which could be a pivotal moment for European space capabilities.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
